_about: Enterprise-readiness plan P0 (docs/architecture/ask-agent/ENTERPRISE_READINESS_PLAN.md §7): multi-turn Ask cases replayed by tools/ask_conversation_eval.py through the live agent path inside a rolled-back transaction. Each case is a REDACTED derivative of a production turn (2026-10-22 audit) or of a client email in the owner's Drive folder (owner ruling O1) - no client, person or company name other than our own brands, no figures that identify a deal. Expectations are mechanical: forbid_brand (no published policy of that brand cited), route (model|fixed), all_points (flag points:x/y with x==y), forbid / require (case-insensitive regexes on the reply). A 'require' that encodes the plan's TARGET behaviour (owner line, brand line, clarifying question) is EXPECTED to fail on today's code - that failure is the baseline.

cases.source: Drive: client MSA review email with 17 points mixing MSA terms and CloudPe items

turns.message:
client sent these before signing the MSA, pls help me reply point wise

1. Contract term & commitment - confirm exact term/minimum commitment; whether at MSA, PO or service level.
2. Early termination - allow termination with 30-60 day written notice, or cap early-termination liability.
3. Auto-renewal - remove automatic renewal; renewal only with mutual written consent.
4. Data retention & ownership - minimum 60-day retention after termination with full data export; customer data and backups remain customer property.
5. Suspension for non-payment - formal grace period and notification before suspension.
6. SLA & support - share SLA (uptime, credits, severity, response/resolution, escalation matrix, maintenance notice).
7. Limitation of liability - carve-outs for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, confidentiality breach, security incidents.
8. Mutual indemnity instead of one-sided indemnity.
9. Refunds & service credits for outages and repeated SLA violations.
10. Security & compliance - confirm controls and certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2).
11. Backup & DR - frequency, retention, RTO/RPO.
12. Migration assistance on exit.
13. CloudPe audit controls - user activity logs, login history, admin action tracking.
14. CloudPe commercial discount - confirm the existing discount is protected for 1 year.
15. 10-15 days prior notice for impacting maintenance.
16. Pricing fixed through the committed tenure.
17. Payment terms - we are MSME registered, request a 45-day payment cycle.

cases.source: owner 2026-10-27: the 50 owner-approved hard questions (hard_retrieval.json) asked in ONE conversation, harder level by level, as a reader types (one line to a pasted email); many turns read only from earlier ones. Each turn cites its question's gold slot, never its must_not; a question our sources do not answer says so

turns.message: Is mining bitcoin on our machines allowed?
aur agar customer apne server pe crypto mining kare toh? same rule hai kya
Do we have to check a customer's ID before we give them service?
ye KYC wala step skip kar sakte hai kya agar customer bahut jaldi me ho?
Which courts decide if there's a dispute with us?
jhagda CloudPe ke customer ke saath ho toh bhi wahi court?
What interest do we charge when an invoice is paid late?
matlab 3 mahine late ho gaya toh kitna interest lagega total?
and for CloudPe customers?
Wait, our internal standard and the Leapswitch website don't give the same rate, do they? Give me both side by side, and tell me which one sales should quote.
If they still don't pay, after how many days can we cut off the server?
The website says 7 days, but does our company standard need notice and a cure period before we suspend? I don't want sales promising something Legal won't back.
Client wrote back on exactly this: 'Suspension for non-payment - formal grace period and notification before suspension.' What do I tell them?
Another point in the same mail: they're MSME registered and want a 45-day payment cycle. Can we agree to that?
Do we give MSME customers any discount?

One more from them, word for word: 'Pricing and payment - LeapSwitch to confirm: (a) prices fixed for the 12-month term; (b) only undisputed invoices payable, disputes within 10 working days; (c) prepaid fees refunded pro rata on our breach or force majeure.' Go point by point please, and keep it short enough to paste into my reply.
How long does someone have to raise a compensation request after downtime?

cite: PUB:PUBLISHED_SLA_LEAPSWITCH:How to Request a Service Credit
PUB:PUBLISHED_SLA_CLOUDPE:How to Request a Service Credit

turns.message: Leapswitch me ye kitne din hai aur CloudPe me kitne?

cite: PUB:PUBLISHED_SLA_*:How to Request a Service Credit

turns.message: For CloudPe specifically — once the downtime is confirmed, how many days until the credit actually shows up?

cite: PUB:PUBLISHED_SLA_CLOUDPE:How to Request a Service Credit

turns.message: And the credit percentage for each uptime band? Same brand.
What doesn't count as downtime for them?
Now switch to Leapswitch: the dedicated server service credit table.
What uptime do they promise for dual power servers?
kitne din pehle maintenance ka notice dete ho, exact hours me batao

Their service-level section, pasted as is: 'Service levels - LeapSwitch to: (a) share the SLA, including how uptime is measured and the service credits; (b) confirm planned maintenance only outside business hours, with prior notice; (c) confirm response and resolution times; (d) confirm that availability below the SLA in 2 consecutive months allows termination without charges.' Which of these can we say yes to from our own documents, and which need someone else to confirm?
Also, who exactly do we escalate a P1 to? They want names.
Can the client walk out halfway through a committed term without paying the rest?
aur agar woh beech me bina notice ke chhod de, toh baaki paisa dena padega kya?
So our position is they pay everything — but does the Contract Act even allow that as a penalty? What does the Act say about penalty clauses?
Bottom line, as a lawyer would put it: is a clause making the customer pay the full remaining contract value actually enforceable in India, or only reasonable compensation?
Client is pushing back on exactly that: 'Early termination - allow termination with 30-60 day written notice, or cap early-termination liability.' How do I answer using our standard?
Different topic. What's the most we'd ever have to pay a client if things go wrong?
matlab total liability maximum kitni hai, saal bhar ki fees?
Compare that company position with the cap in the Leapswitch terms of service — same or different?
Do we need to carry professional indemnity insurance, and for how much?

After termination, how long can a customer take their data out under our MSA standard, and what do the website terms say happens to data on terminated services? I need both, because the client quoted the website to me.
They also want this: 'Data retention & ownership - minimum 60-day retention after termination with full data export; customer data and backups remain customer property.'
Can they come and physically audit our data centre?
How quickly must a cyber incident be reported to the government?
data breach hua toh CERT-In ko kitne ghante me batana hai, aur customer ko bhi batana padega kya?
Is there a separate duty under the DPDP Act to tell the Data Protection Board?
And if the personal data leaked because our security was weak, what compensation can the client claim under Indian law?

Their security ask, verbatim: 'Security - LeapSwitch to confirm encryption at rest and in transit, MFA for admin access, access logs retained in India for 180 days, incident notification within 6 hours and a root cause analysis within 5 business days.' Tell me what our documents already commit to and what they don't.
Are we ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certified? Same thread, they asked that too.

Last block of their mail: 'Disaster recovery - LeapSwitch to confirm: (a) that DR is added to the Service Scope; (b) a committed RPO of 1 hour and RTO of 4 hours; (c) DR invocation on failure, cyber incident or the client's request, with failback without data loss; (d) DR drills twice a year, with a written report.'
So what RPO and RTO do we actually commit to?
Going back to the start of this chat: if this client decides to cancel instead, how do they stop the subscription, and when does it actually end?
And force majeure: after how many days can either side terminate under our MSA position versus the terms of service?
Where must arbitration be seated, and which Act governs it?

Last one. One of our engineers signed a non-compete governed by Delaware law with a US company before joining us, and the client's lawyer raised it on a call today. Is that non-compete enforceable against our staff?
